9	/-!
10	# The `n`-fold tensor power is the `n`-ary coproduct of algebras
11	
12	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean` lists four inputs a `Scheme.GlueData` for `Sym^n C`
13	needs. Item 3 is the comparison
14	
15	> the `n`-ary coproduct of `R`-algebras **is** the `n`-fold tensor power `⨂[R] i, A i`,
16	
17	which two previous sessions on this leg recorded as absent from mathlib and unbuilt in AJC,
18	with the consequence that `SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` (whose diagram is built
19	from the `n`-ary **coproduct** in `Under k`) and the whole `PiTensorProduct` layer
20	(`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean`, `SymPowInvariants*.lean`) were provably *about different
21	objects*. That mismatch is what this file removes.
22	
23	## What was actually missing, and what was not
24	
25	Mathlib has the **binary** case as a pushout (`CommRingCat.pushoutCoconeIsColimit`,
26	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Ring/Constructions.lean`) and nothing `n`-ary. But it turns out that
27	*both halves of the `n`-ary universal property are already in mathlib*, unbundled and not
28	labelled as a colimit:
29	
30	* **uniqueness** is `PiTensorProduct.algHom_ext` — two algebra maps out of a finite tensor
31	  power agree as soon as they agree on each `PiTensorProduct.singleAlgHom i`, the inclusion
32	  `a ↦ 1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ 1`. That is exactly `Cofan.IsColimit`'s uniqueness clause;
33	* **existence** is one application of `PiTensorProduct.liftAlgHom` to the multilinear map
34	  `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`, and is `coprodLift` below.
35	
36	So the honest description of item 3 is not "mathlib lacks the `n`-ary comparison" but "mathlib
37	has it in pieces, under names that do not mention colimits". The only mathematical content
38	supplied here is the multilinearity of `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`, which is
39	`Finset.prod_update_of_mem` three times.
40	
41	**Where commutativity is load-bearing.** `coprodLift` needs the target `S` to be
42	*commutative*: the product `∏ i, f i (x i)` must be independent of the order of the factors,
43	and multiplicativity `f (x * y) = f x * f y` is `Finset.prod_mul_distrib`. This is why the
44	statement is about the coproduct in **commutative** algebras — which is the category the
45	affine symmetric power lives in — and not a coproduct in all `R`-algebras, where the tensor
46	power is *not* the coproduct. A reader coming from the noncommutative case should not read
47	this file as more general than it is.
48	
49	## Main results
50	
51	* `PiTensorProduct.coprodLift` — the lift of a family `f : ∀ i, A i →ₐ[R] S` into a
52	  commutative `S`, together with `coprodLift_tprod` and
53	  `coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom` (its defining equation).
54	* `PiTensorProduct.existsUnique_coprodLift` — the `n`-ary coproduct universal property as a
55	  single `∃!` statement: this is the form a colimit consumer wants.
56	* `PiTensorProduct.coprodLift_permAlgHom` — **the equivariance that item 3 actually asks
57	  for**, and the reason this file imports `SymPowTensorAction`: the comparison intertwines
58	  the factor-permutation action `permAlgHom` on the tensor power with *reindexing the family*.
59	  Without it the identification would be an isomorphism of objects that does not respect the
60	  `S_n`-actions, and so would say nothing about symmetric powers (the failure mode recorded
61	  in this leg's memory as "groups agree ≠ maps agree").
62	
63	## What this does *not* close
64	
65	Item 3 of the four-item bill, only. In particular:
66	
67	* it does **not** build the `Under k`-valued or `CommRingCat`-valued cofan and prove
68	  `IsColimit` of it. The algebra-level `∃!` is the mathematical content; crossing into
69	  `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` is bookkeeping this file deliberately leaves to its consumer, since
70	  `SymPowColimit`'s §5 caveat about which category is which is exactly where a previous
71	  session went wrong;
72	* `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` for the curve remains open, and `AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six
73	  sorries are unchanged.
74	
75	## References
76	
77	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94 (the affine symmetric power
78	`(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`). Mathlib's binary comparison:
79	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Ring/Constructions.lean`.
80	-/

88	namespace PiTensorProduct
89	
90	section Coproduct
91	
92	variable {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} {A : ι → Type w} {S : Type*}
93	  [CommRing R] [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (A i)] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
94	
95	section Mk
96	
97	variable [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
98	
99	omit [Fintype ι] in
100	/-- **Postcomposing a family of algebra maps commutes with `Function.update`.** The one
101	bookkeeping fact behind multilinearity of `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`: changing the `i`-th entry of
102	the tuple changes the `i`-th factor of the product and nothing else. -/
103	private theorem comp_update (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (x : ∀ i, A i) (i : ι) (v : A i) :
104	    (fun j => f j (Function.update x i v j))
105	      = Function.update (fun j => f j (x j)) i (f i v) := by
106	  funext j
107	  by_cases hj : j = i
108	  · subst hj; simp
109	  · simp [Function.update_of_ne hj]
110	
111	/-- **The multilinear map underlying the coproduct lift**, `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`.
112	
113	Both multilinearity clauses are `comp_update` followed by `Finset.prod_update_of_mem`, which
114	isolates the `i`-th factor; then `map_add` / `map_smul` of `f i` and distributivity. -/
115	noncomputable def coprodMultilinear (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) :
116	    MultilinearMap R A S :=
117	  MultilinearMap.mk (fun x => ∏ i, f i (x i))
118	    (by
119	      intro _ x i a b
120	      rw [comp_update f x i (a + b), comp_update f x i a, comp_update f x i b,
121	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i),
122	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i),
123	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i), map_add, add_mul])
124	    (by
125	      intro _ x i c a
126	      rw [comp_update f x i (c • a), comp_update f x i a,
127	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i),
128	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i), map_smul, smul_mul_assoc])
129	
130	omit [DecidableEq ι] in
131	@[simp]
132	theorem coprodMultilinear_apply (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (x : ∀ i, A i) :
133	    coprodMultilinear f x = ∏ i, f i (x i) := rfl
134	
135	/-- **The coproduct lift.** A family of algebra maps `f i : A i →ₐ[R] S` into a
136	*commutative* `S` induces an algebra map out of the tensor power, sending
137	`a_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a_n` to `f_1(a_1) ⋯ f_n(a_n)`.
138	
139	Unitality is `∏ i, f i 1 = 1`; multiplicativity is `Finset.prod_mul_distrib`, and **this is
140	where commutativity of `S` is used** — see the module header. -/
141	noncomputable def coprodLift (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) :
142	    (⨂[R] i, A i) →ₐ[R] S :=
143	  liftAlgHom (coprodMultilinear f)
144	    (by simp)
145	    (by
146	      intro x y
147	      simp only [coprodMultilinear_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, Finset.prod_mul_distrib])
148	
149	omit [DecidableEq ι] in
150	@[simp]
151	theorem coprodLift_tprod (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (x : ∀ i, A i) :
152	    coprodLift f (tprod R x) = ∏ i, f i (x i) := by
153	  simp [coprodLift]
154	
155	/-- **The defining equation of the coproduct lift.** Precomposing with the `i`-th structural
156	inclusion `singleAlgHom i` recovers `f i`: every factor other than the `i`-th contributes
157	`f j 1 = 1`. -/
158	theorem coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (i : ι) :
159	    (coprodLift f).comp (singleAlgHom i) = f i := by
160	  ext a
161	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, coprodLift_tprod]
162	  have h : (fun j => f j (MonoidHom.mulSingle A i a j))
163	      = Function.update (fun _ => (1 : S)) i (f i a) := by
164	    funext j
165	    by_cases hj : j = i
166	    · subst hj; simp
167	    · simp [Function.update_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hj]
168	  rw [h, Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i)]
169	  simp
170	
171	set_option linter.unusedFintypeInType false in
172	/-- **The `n`-ary coproduct universal property of the tensor power, as one statement.**
173	
174	For a finite family of commutative `R`-algebras `A i` and a commutative `R`-algebra `S`,
175	algebra maps out of `⨂[R] i, A i` correspond to families of algebra maps out of the `A i`:
176	there is a *unique* `u` with `u ∘ singleAlgHom i = f i` for every `i`.
177	
178	This is the shape a `Cofan.IsColimit` consumer wants. Existence is `coprodLift`; uniqueness
179	is mathlib's `algHom_ext`, which is the coproduct uniqueness clause under another name.
180	
181	The `[Fintype ι]` binder does not appear in the statement's *type* (the linter says so) but is
182	load-bearing in the proof: `coprodLift`'s product `∏ i, f i (x i)` needs it. `Finite` would do
183	after `Fintype.ofFinite`, but then the witness would not be syntactically `coprodLift f`, which
184	is what call sites rewrite with. -/
185	theorem existsUnique_coprodLift (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) :
186	    ∃! u : (⨂[R] i, A i) →ₐ[R] S, ∀ i, u.comp (singleAlgHom i) = f i :=
187	  ⟨coprodLift f, coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom f,
188	    fun _ hu => algHom_ext fun i => (hu i).trans (coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom f i).symm⟩
189	
190	end Mk
191	
192	/-! ### Equivariance: the comparison respects the `S_n`-actions
193	
194	The identification above is an isomorphism of *objects*. For the symmetric power it must also
195	match the actions on the two sides — otherwise it is the "groups agree but the maps do not"
196	failure this project has hit before, and it would license nothing about `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`.
197	
198	The statement is the natural one: permuting the factors of the tensor power and then lifting
199	`f` is the same as lifting the *reindexed* family. Since all the `A i` are the same algebra
200	`A` in the symmetric-power application, "reindexed family" is just `f ∘ e`. -/
201	
202	section Equivariance
203	
204	-- `A'` must live in the *ring's* universe `u`: `SymPowTensorAction.permAlgHom` is stated with
205	-- `(R : Type u) (A : Type u)`, so a `Type w` algebra cannot be permuted by it. Matching the
206	-- binder here rather than generalising `permAlgHom` keeps this file additive over that one.
207	-- No `DecidableEq ι`: the proof opens with `classical`, so it would be an unused binder in the
208	-- statement (and the linter rightly rejects it).
209	variable {A' : Type u} [CommRing A'] [Algebra R A'] [Fintype ι]
210	
211	/-- **The comparison is equivariant.** For a constant family `A' i = A'`, permuting the
212	tensor factors along `e` and then lifting `f` agrees with lifting the family reindexed along
213	`e⁻¹`:
214	
215	`coprodLift f ∘ permAlgHom e = coprodLift (f ∘ e⁻¹)`.
216	
217	**Read the variance, and do not guess it.** The first draft of this lemma stated `f ∘ e` on
218	the right and was *false*: the residual goal was `f (e⁻¹ i) a = f (e i) a`, which holds only
219	at an involution. On generators, `permAlgHom e` sends `tprod x` to `tprod (x ∘ e)`, so the
220	lift becomes `∏ i, f i (x (e i))`; reindexing `j = e i` turns that into
221	`∏ j, f (e⁻¹ j) (x j)`, which is the lift of `f ∘ e⁻¹`. The inverse here is the *same*
222	`permAlgHom` anti-homomorphism bookkeeping that `SymPowTensorAction.permAlgHom_comp` records
223	and that `permMulSemiringAction` absorbs by acting through `σ⁻¹`.
224	
225	This is the clause that makes the identification usable for symmetric powers rather than
226	merely true: without it the two sides carry unrelated `S_n`-actions, and an isomorphism of
227	objects alone licenses nothing about `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`. -/
228	theorem coprodLift_permAlgHom (f : ι → (A' →ₐ[R] S)) (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
229	    (coprodLift (A := fun _ : ι => A') f).comp (permAlgHom R A' e)
230	      = coprodLift (A := fun _ : ι => A') (fun i => f (e.symm i)) := by
231	  classical
232	  refine algHom_ext fun i => ?_
233	  ext a
234	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, permAlgHom_tprod,
235	    coprodLift_tprod, AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, coprodLift_tprod]
236	  -- Both sides are a product with a single nontrivial factor; identify which slot.
237	  have hl : (fun j => f j (MonoidHom.mulSingle (fun _ : ι => A') i a (e j)))
238	      = Function.update (fun _ => (1 : S)) (e.symm i) (f (e.symm i) a) := by
239	    funext j
240	    by_cases hj : j = e.symm i
241	    · subst hj; simp
242	    · have hne : e j ≠ i := fun hc => hj (by rw [← hc, Equiv.symm_apply_apply])
243	      simp [Function.update_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hne]
244	  have hr : (fun j => f (e.symm j) (MonoidHom.mulSingle (fun _ : ι => A') i a j))
245	      = Function.update (fun _ => (1 : S)) i (f (e.symm i) a) := by
246	    funext j
247	    by_cases hj : j = i
248	    · subst hj; simp
249	    · simp [Function.update_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hj]
250	  rw [hl, hr, Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _),
251	    Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i)]
252	  simp
253	
254	end Equivariance
255	
256	end Coproduct
257	
258	end PiTensorProduct

6	import Mathlib

8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.GrpObjFoldSum
9	
10	/-!
11	# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action
12	
13	`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
14	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
15	needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
16	stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
17	quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
18	`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
19	
20	That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
21	it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.
22	
23	## What was actually going on
24	
25	`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
26	for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
27	a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
28	the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
29	`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
30	`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
31	`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.
32	
33	So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
34	data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
35	generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
36	copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
37	being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
38	direction that should go.
39	
40	## Main results
41	
42	* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
43	  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
44	* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
45	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
46	  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
47	  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
48	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` — **the `S_n` instantiation**: for `C` a `k̄`-scheme, every
49	  point of `C^n` has an `S_n`-stable affine open neighbourhood, given the orbit hypothesis.
50	
51	**Correction (2026-07-29): the `S_n` producer exists and this file's scope note said it did
52	not.** Two earlier revisions ran in opposite directions and both were wrong. One advertised a
53	`permAction : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut (C^n)` that did not exist; the correction then
54	recorded building it as blocked, on the grounds that `MonObj.permAut` "is a bare morphism
55	never shown to be an isomorphism" and `SymPowColimit.permEnd` "lands in `End`, not `Aut`".
56	Both grounds were accurate statements about the tree and the inference from them was not:
57	`permAut C σ⁻¹` is a two-sided inverse of `permAut C σ`, because
58	`permAut C σ ≫ permAut C τ = permAut C (σ * τ)`. That is `MonObj.permAut_comp`, and the
59	action is `MonObj.permAutHom`, both now in `Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean` — four lines, no
60	construction. The lesson is the `permEnd` convention: the inverse `permEnd` carries is forced
61	by `End`'s reversed multiplication, and reading it as a fact about `permAut` is what made an
62	isomorphism look absent.
63	
64	## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis
65	
66	The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
67	characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
68	`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
69	through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.
70	
71	## Scope — what this does and does not give
72	
73	**Does**: prove the stable-cover statement at the generality a glue-data construction wants —
74	a *finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms*, with no Galois hypothesis and no
75	characteristic hypothesis.
76	
77	**Does** now also apply it to `S_n` acting on `C^n` — `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` below,
78	via `MonObj.permAutHom`. See the correction in the main-results list: the two previous
79	revisions of this section, in both directions, were wrong about that.
80	
81	**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open and
82	`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged. Counting honestly, a glue-data assembly needs
83	*four* things and this file now supplies two of them:
84	
85	1. ✓ a `G`-stable affine cover — below;
86	2. ✓ the `Aut`-valued `S_n`-action — `MonObj.permAutHom`, and its instantiation here;
87	3. the identification of the `n`-fold coproduct of algebras with the `n`-fold tensor power,
88	   matching its permutation action to `PiTensorProduct.permAlgHom` — mathlib has only the
89	   *binary* case (`Algebra/Category/Ring/Constructions.lean`), and nothing in AJC builds the
90	   `n`-ary one. Without it the affine layer of `Albanese/SymPowInvariantsUnder.lean` and
91	   `SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` are about different objects;
92	4. the cocycle/overlap agreement of the chart quotients, plus `OrbitsInAffineOpen` **for the
93	   curve** — where quasi-projectivity would enter, and mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
94	   vocabulary at this pin.
95	
96	Nothing consumes this file yet, and item 2 is why: it is not wired in, and it cannot be until
97	that action exists.
98	
99	## References
100	
101	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94. EGA II 4.5.4 for the
102	orbit-in-affine hypothesis. The original proof is
103	`AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction.exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`
104	(`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:193`), whose supporting lemmas
105	(`exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite`, `mem_finset_inf`, `preimage_finset_inf`,
106	`basicOpen_finset_prod`) are imported and reused unchanged.
107	-/
108	
109	set_option autoImplicit false
110	
111	universe w u
112	
113	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
114	
115	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
116	
117	namespace StableGroupAction
118	
119	-- The group's universe `w` is **independent** of the scheme's universe `u`. The proof only
120	-- ever indexes a `Finset.univ` by `G`, and the underlying prime-avoidance lemma
121	-- `exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite` is already polymorphic in its index type (`{ι : Type*}`), so
122	-- nothing forces `G : Type u`. Keeping them tied — as the first draft did, copying the Galois
123	-- statement where `G = Gal(L/K)` happens to live in `Type u` — makes the theorem inapplicable
124	-- to `Equiv.Perm (Fin n) : Type 0`, which is precisely the group the symmetric power needs.
125	variable {G : Type w} [Group G] [Finite G] {X : Scheme.{u}} (act : G →* Aut X)
126	
127	/-- **Orbit-in-affine hypothesis for a bare action** (EGA II 4.5.4): every orbit is contained
128	in an affine open. This hypothesis is *essential*, not a convenience — without it the
129	quotient need only be an algebraic space (Hironaka; see `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`'s
130	module docstring). It holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
131	at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by hand. -/
132	def OrbitsInAffineOpen : Prop :=
133	  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ g : G, (act g).hom.base x ∈ U.1
134	
135	/-- A `G`-stable open of `X`. -/
136	def IsStableOpen (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
137	  ∀ g : G, (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U
138	
139	omit [Finite G] in
140	/-- The identity acts as the identity. This and `act_mul_hom` are the *only* structural facts
141	the main theorem uses about the action — both are `map_one`/`map_mul` of the `MonoidHom`,
142	which is why no semilinearity is needed. -/
143	lemma act_one_hom : (act 1).hom = 𝟙 X := by rw [map_one]; rfl
144	
145	omit [Finite G] in
146	/-- Multiplicativity, in the composition order `Aut` gives. -/
147	lemma act_mul_hom (g t : G) : (act (g * t)).hom = (act t).hom ≫ (act g).hom := by
148	  rw [map_mul]; rfl
149	
150	/-- **The `G`-stable affine neighbourhood theorem, for a bare finite group action.**
151	
152	Under the orbit-in-affine hypothesis, every point has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood.
153	
154	The argument, in three moves: prime avoidance (`exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite`) puts the whole
155	orbit of `x` inside a basic open `D(s)` contained in `W = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹U`; the **norm**
156	`N = ∏_g g(s)|_W` then satisfies `D(N) = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ D(s)`, which is `G`-stable by
157	reindexing the intersection; and `D(N) ⊆ D(s) ⊆ U` is affine as a basic open of an affine.
158	Stability is proved at the level of *opens*, which is what avoids transporting sections along
159	the action isomorphisms.
160	
161	The norm is a product, so no `1/|G|` appears and the statement is characteristic-free.
162	
163	**Provenance.** This is `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:193` with its `SemilinearGalAction`
164	binder replaced by `G →* Aut X` and `[Fintype G]`; the proof term is otherwise unchanged, which
165	is the evidence that the semilinearity field was never load-bearing. See the module header. -/
166	theorem exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits (h : OrbitsInAffineOpen act) (x : X) :
167	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ IsStableOpen act U := by
168	  classical
169	  -- `[Finite G]` is the honest binder; the `Fintype` is an artefact of `Finset.univ`.
170	  letI : Fintype G := Fintype.ofFinite G
171	  obtain ⟨U, hxU⟩ := h x
172	  -- the whole orbit meets every translated chart: `g(t(x)) = (g*t)(x) ∈ U`.
173	  have horb : ∀ t g : G, (act g).hom.base ((act t).hom.base x) ∈ U.1 := by
174	    intro t g
175	    have hh : (act g).hom.base ((act t).hom.base x) = (act (g * t)).hom.base x := by
176	      rw [act_mul_hom act g t]; rfl
177	    rw [hh]; exact hxU (g * t)
178	  -- prime avoidance: `orbit ⊆ D(s) ⊆ W := ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ U`.
179	  obtain ⟨s, hs_mem, hs_le⟩ := exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
180	    (fun g : G => (act g).hom.base x) hxU
181	    (V := Finset.univ.inf fun g : G => (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
182	    (fun t => mem_finset_inf.mpr fun g _ => horb t g)
183	  have hWle : ∀ g : G,
184	      (Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ≤ (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1 :=
185	    fun g => Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)
186	  -- the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)|_W` and its factors
187	  set t : G → Γ(X, Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :=
188	    fun g => X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle g)).op ((act g).hom.app U.1 s) with ht
189	  set N : Γ(X, Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) := ∏ g : G, t g with hN
190	  -- each factor cuts out the corresponding translate of `D(s)` inside `W`
191	  have hbo_t : ∀ g : G, X.basicOpen (t g) =
192	      (Finset.univ.inf fun d : G => (act d).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ⊓ (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
193	    intro g
194	    rw [ht, Scheme.basicOpen_res, ← Scheme.preimage_basicOpen]
195	  -- the `g = 1` translate is `D(s)` itself
196	  have hP1 : (act (1 : G)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s = X.basicOpen s := by
197	    rw [act_one_hom act]; rfl
198	  -- `D(N) = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ D(s)`
199	  have hbo_N : X.basicOpen N = Finset.univ.inf fun g : G => (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
200	    rw [hN, basicOpen_finset_prod ⟨1, Finset.mem_univ 1⟩,
201	      Finset.inf_congr rfl fun g _ => hbo_t g]
202	    refine le_antisymm
203	      (Finset.le_inf fun g _ => (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)).trans inf_le_right)
204	      (Finset.le_inf fun g _ => le_inf (le_trans ?_ hs_le)
205	        (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)))
206	    exact le_of_le_of_eq (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ 1)) hP1
207	  -- `D(N) ⊆ D(s)` (the `g = 1` factor)
208	  have hNs : X.basicOpen N ≤ X.basicOpen s := by
209	    rw [hbo_N]
210	    exact le_of_le_of_eq (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ 1)) hP1
211	  refine ⟨X.basicOpen N, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
212	  · -- affineness: `D(N)` is a basic open of the affine `D(s)`
213	    have heq : X.basicOpen (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hs_le).op N) = X.basicOpen N := by
214	      rw [Scheme.basicOpen_res]
215	      exact inf_eq_right.mpr hNs
216	    rw [← heq]
217	    exact (U.2.basicOpen s).basicOpen _
218	  · -- membership: prime avoidance put the whole orbit in `D(s)`
219	    rw [hbo_N, mem_finset_inf]
220	    intro g _
221	    change (act g).hom.base x ∈ X.basicOpen s
222	    exact hs_mem g
223	  · -- stability, at the level of opens: preimage functoriality plus reindexing
224	    intro tau
225	    rw [hbo_N, preimage_finset_inf]
226	    have hPt : ∀ g : G, (act tau).hom ⁻¹ᵁ ((act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s)
227	        = (act (g * tau)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
228	      intro g
229	      rw [act_mul_hom act]; rfl
230	    rw [Finset.inf_congr rfl fun g _ => hPt g]
231	    refine le_antisymm (Finset.le_inf fun d _ => ?_) (Finset.le_inf fun d _ => ?_)
232	    · have hh := Finset.inf_le (s := Finset.univ)
233	        (f := fun g : G => (act (g * tau)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s)
234	        (Finset.mem_univ (d * tau⁻¹))
235	      rwa [inv_mul_cancel_right] at hh
236	    · exact Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ (d * tau))
237	
238	end StableGroupAction
239	
240	/-! ## The `S_n` instantiation
241	
242	The theorem above is stated for a bare `G →* Aut X`. The producer for `G = S_n`,
243	`X = C^n` is `MonObj.permAutHom` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`), so the instantiation is
244	a one-line application. `Scheme` is cartesian monoidal with finite products
245	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Limits`), which is what lets `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)` and `permAut` be
246	formed here at all.
247	
248	This is item 2 of the four-item glue-data bill in the module header, and its being available
249	is what makes item 1 consumable rather than free-standing. -/
250	
251	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
252	
253	/-- **Every point of `C^n` has an `S_n`-stable affine open neighbourhood.**
254	
255	The `S_n`-equivariant form of `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits`, obtained by feeding it
256	the action `MonObj.permAutHom C n`. The orbit hypothesis is unchanged and still has to be
257	supplied for the curve — that is item 4 of the glue-data bill, where quasi-projectivity
258	would enter — but the *equivariance* half is now discharged.
259	
260	Note what is and is not claimed: this gives the stable charts a `Scheme.GlueData` for
261	`Sym^n C` would be built on. It does not build that glue data, and `HasColimit
262	(permDiagram C n)` remains open. -/
263	theorem exists_stable_affineOpen_perm (C : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ)
264	    (h : StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen (MonObj.permAutHom C n))
265	    (x : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) : Scheme.{u})) :
266	    ∃ U : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) : Scheme.{u}).Opens,
267	      IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen (MonObj.permAutHom C n) U :=
268	  StableGroupAction.exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits (MonObj.permAutHom C n) h x

namespace CategoryTheory

open Limits

/-- **A one-object diagram's sections are its invariants.** For a diagram indexed by
`SingleObj G`, lying in the `sections` set is equivalent to being fixed by every `g : G` —
the many-object quantifier collapses because the index category has one object and
`SingleObj.toEnd` is an equivalence onto its endomorphisms.

**What this is for, stated so it does not overclaim.** It is the reason to *expect* that the
affine colimit is `Spec` of the invariant subring of the `n`-fold tensor power — Milne's
`(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` in III.3 Proposition 3.1 — because limits in `CommRingCat` are computed as
sections (`CommRingCat.limitCone`) and, by this lemma, a one-object diagram's sections are
its fixed points.

It is **not** a proof of that identification: the statement below is about
`SingleObj G ⥤ Type` and mentions neither `CommRingCat` nor `Spec` nor a tensor power. So
the carrier is *not* named in Lean; see the §5 header. An earlier version of this docstring
claimed it was, which is why the caveat is spelled out here rather than only there. -/
theorem mem_sections_singleObj_iff {G : Type u} [Group G] (F : SingleObj G ⥤ Type v)
    (x : (j : SingleObj G) → F.obj j) :
    x ∈ F.sections ↔
      ∀ g : G, F.map (SingleObj.toEnd G g) (x (SingleObj.star G)) = x (SingleObj.star G) := by
  refine ⟨fun hx g => hx (SingleObj.toEnd G g), fun h j j' f => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star G := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  obtain rfl : j' = SingleObj.star G := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  exact h ((SingleObj.toEnd G).symm f)

/-- **Every `n`, in `Type`.** The symmetric power interface with its symmetry hypothesis,
inhabited at all `n` — `Type` has all colimits.

Contrast with `symPowDataOne`: that was `n = 1` only. Here `n` is arbitrary, so the
statements the Albanese argument quantifies over are non-vacuous in the range where the
group-law step is genuinely exercised. -/
theorem symPowData_type (X : Type u) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ D : SymPowData X n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      MonObj.permAut X σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
  symPowData_of_hasColimit X n

/-- **Every `n`, in the opposite of `k`-algebras** — the affine algebra case.

`(Under k)ᵒᵖ` has all colimits (they are limits in `Under k`), so the pair `(D, hproj)` is
inhabited there at every `n`, with no construction written.

**What this is and is not.** It is the inhabitation statement. It is *not* a formalisation
of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1's affine half, which also identifies the object: morally

`AffineScheme.equivCommRingCat`) and the carrier is `Spec` of the invariant subring of the
`n`-fold tensor power — but neither bridge is built here. `mem_sections_singleObj_iff` is
the reason to expect the second; it is not a proof of it. See the §5 header. -/

    letI : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Under k)ᵒᵖ := ofHasFiniteProducts

`Over (Spec k̄)`

The Albanese connector lives in `Over (Spec k̄)`, so one might expect the missing
construction to be an over-category one, with structure-map bookkeeping on top of the
quotient. It is not: `Over.forget` **creates** colimits, so a colimit of the permutation
action in `Scheme` gives one in `Over (Spec k̄)` for free.

That removes a whole layer from the remaining work: the leg's single open obligation is
`HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` — one diagram, for the curve at hand — and by
`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` that is exactly equivalent to the datum the Albanese theorems
consume.

**Do not strengthen it to `HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) Scheme`.**
That form is tempting because it reads as "schemes have finite-group quotients", but it is
strictly stronger, it is *not* what the equivalence covers, and by the availability table
below it is believed false at this pin — so a theorem carrying it would be vacuously true
and its obligation undischargeable in principle. The per-diagram binder is satisfiable and
is the honest residue. `symPowData_over_of_scheme_colimits` below is stated with the
quantified form deliberately, as a *sufficient* condition and nothing more.

**What is and is not available for it, measured at this pin** (so the next session does not
re-derive the search):

* `HasCoproducts Scheme` — **available**. So the disjoint-union half of any glueing is free.
* `HasCoequalizers Scheme`, `HasPushouts Scheme` — **not available**, neither synthesizes.
  This is the actual obstruction: a colimit over `SingleObj G` is a coequalizer-type colimit,
  and schemes do not admit them in general (the quotient of a scheme by an equivalence
  relation need not be a scheme — cf. the standing caveat in inbox `I-0074` about
  algebraic spaces).

  tool Milne's affine-and-glue route would use: build the affine quotients (done here, at

quotients". It is: assemble a `Scheme.GlueData` from the affine quotients of

inputs now exist.

**One sharpening, because it is exactly where the affine result stops.** `Scheme.Spec` is
fully faithful and preserves limits, so the affine quotient's universal property transfers

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

/-- **The curve case reduces to `Scheme`.** If `Scheme` has colimits of the
`S_n`-action shape, then the pair the Albanese theorems quantify over exists for any
`k̄`-scheme `C` — in particular for a proper curve.

structure morphism has to be checked. Compare `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`'s

strictly stronger than `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` and believed false at this pin (§6),

content — it is what shows the over-category layer costs nothing — and it is stated in the
strong form because that is the form in which "schemes have finite-group quotients" would
arrive. The obligation to discharge is the per-diagram one. -/
theorem symPowData_over_of_scheme_colimits {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) (n : ℕ)
    [HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) Scheme.{u}] :
    ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
  symPowData_of_hasColimit C n

end AlgebraicGeometry
